outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the conjecture has been claimed for n = 16 (Kafidov, arXiv 21 Jul 2026, whose author disclosed that GPT-5.6 Sol through ChatGPT produced the proof strategy and most of the text), for every n ≥ 17 (Pang, arXiv 1 Jun 2026), for n = 4 (Li, Xiong and Yang, arXiv 31 Jul 2026, via an exact sum-of-squares certificate checked in Lean), and for n = 5 (an AI-generated GitHub candidate, 5–6 Aug 2026, whose maintainer says nobody qualified has validated it); none of these has been refereed in any source I could find, and the general conjecture for all n remains open.
problem_asks: (1) For each n (the Wikipedia wording gives no range; the literature states it for every n ≥ 2): the set K_n of n×n matrices with nonnegative real entries whose entries sum to n. (2) The function φ(A) = (product of the row sums of A) + (product of the column sums of A) − per(A), where per is the permanent. (3) That φ attains a maximum over K_n. (4) That the maximum is attained exactly at A = J_n/n, the matrix with every entry 1/n, i.e. uniquely there. The literature's value of the maximum is 2 − n!/n^n; it is not in the Wikipedia wording but follows from (4). Parts (3) and (4) are both asked: the value and the uniqueness of the maximiser. Equivalent normalisation (total sum 1, entries 1/n²) is used in some sources and is the same problem.

events.what_happened: Sinkhorn is credited with proving the conjecture for n = 2 (every φ-maximising matrix on K_2 is J_2/2). The attribution is in the 2023 arXiv abstract of Divya and Somasundaram (arXiv 2312.00464) and in the 2026 Pang preprint's bibliography, which cites 'Sinkhorn (1984)' for the n = 2 case as read through a summary of the HTML. I did not locate Sinkhorn's paper, so the year is a secondary citation and the journal and month are unknown.
events.delivers: The full conjecture for n = 2 (that J_2/2 is the unique maximiser of φ on K_2).

checked_by.qualification: Original author of the n = 2 argument
checked_by.what_they_did: Proved the n = 2 case (per secondary citations only)

events.directly_checkable: The n = 2 case is a two-variable inequality on a 2×2 matrix with entry sum 2 and can be checked by hand; I did not do so.
events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjectured maximiser J_2/2, for n = 2 only.

events.what_happened: Hwang showed the conjecture holds for positive semidefinite symmetric matrices in K_n and for matrices in a sufficiently small neighbourhood of J_n/n. This is reported in the 2023 arXiv review by Divya and Somasundaram (arXiv 2312.00464) as read through its abstract and summary, and in the Pang bibliography as 'Hwang1986' and 'Hwang1987'. I could not confirm which of the two years carries this result, and I did not open Hwang's paper, so no date can be given.
events.delivers: The conjecture for positive semidefinite symmetric matrices in K_n (for every n that such matrices cover), and for matrices in a neighbourhood of J_n/n in K_n whose size is not given in the sources. This is a restricted class, not a full case for any n.
events.remains: All non-semidefinite matrices in K_n for every n, and the neighbourhood-free statement for every n.

checked_by.what_they_did: Proved the restricted statements (per secondary description only)

events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjectured maximiser, on restricted classes only.

events.what_happened: Hwang is credited with proving the conjecture for n = 3. The attribution appears in the 2023 Divya–Somasundaram abstract and in the Pang bibliography (Hwang 1986 and 1987, 'the case n = 3'). A 1987 Linear Algebra and its Applications paper titled 'On a conjecture of E. Dittert' is cited by a search summary; the search index did not return it, so I could not open it or confirm the title and volume.

checked_by.who: S. G. Hwang; Linear Algebra and its Applications (per secondary citation)
checked_by.qualification: Author; refereed journal of record if the citation is correct
checked_by.what_they_did: Proved the n = 3 case (per secondary citation only)

events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjectured maximiser J_3/3, for n = 3 only.

events.what_happened: Cheon and Wanless, 'Some results towards the Dittert conjecture on permanents', Linear Algebra and its Applications (DOI 10.1016/j.laa.2010.08.041). The journal year is 2012 per Wikipedia's citation; the DOI suffix suggests the work was submitted or accepted around 2010, and the first public version was not established. Per a search summary of the 2024 Special Matrices paper, they showed that a partly decomposable A in K_n has φ(A) < φ(J_n/n), and that a matrix whose zeros form a block is not φ-maximising. The Monash PDF of the paper was unreadable through the tool, so the summary is unconfirmed. The ANU record shows keyword 'doubly superstochastic' and 'partly decomposable' and a restriction until 2037.
events.delivers: Partial result: partly decomposable matrices in K_n are not maximisers (φ(A) < φ(J_n/n) for them), and matrices whose zeros form a block are not maximisers. It excludes a class of candidates; it does not identify the maximiser within the fully indecomposable class.
events.remains: The maximiser must be fully indecomposable; the uniqueness and value claims for every n remain open.

checked_by.who: Gi-Sang Cheon and Ian M. Wanless; Linear Algebra and its Applications (Elsevier)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the partial results (journal acceptance; content per search summary)

events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjectured maximiser, by excluding partly decomposable and block-zero matrices.

events.what_happened: Hwang, Sohn and Kim, 'The Dittert's function on a set of nonnegative matrices', International Journal of Mathematics and Mathematical Sciences 13(4), pp. 709–716 (received 6 Nov 1989, revised 12 Jan 1990). The abstract says the paper 'investigates some properties of a certain subclass of K_n related to the function φ and the Dittert's conjecture'. It does not claim any case of the conjecture is settled.
events.delivers: Properties of an unspecified subclass of K_n related to φ. No case of the conjecture is claimed as settled by the abstract.
events.remains: The conjecture for every n, and for all of K_n.

checked_by.who: Suk Geun Hwang, Mun-Gu Sohn, Si-Ju Kim; International Journal of Mathematics and Mathematical Sciences

events.direction: Neutral to the question as stated; it studies a subclass and does not settle a case.

events.what_happened: 'On the monotonicity of the Dittert function on classes of nonnegative matrices', Bulletin of the Korean Mathematical Society 30(2), pp. 265–275, 1993, per a search result. It studies whether φ is monotone on the segment from A in K_n to J_n/n, and gives a sufficient condition on A (including a Dokovic-inequality condition) under which monotonicity holds, and a subclass where it holds. The authors were not confirmed from the search result, and I did not open the paper.
events.delivers: A monotonicity statement along the segment from A to J_n/n for a sufficient-condition class of A, and a subclass with the property. It is a generalisation of the conjecture to a monotonicity question, not a settlement of it.
events.remains: The conjecture itself for every n.

checked_by.who: Bulletin of the Korean Mathematical Society (authors not confirmed)

events.direction: Neutral; a monotonicity result on a class of matrices.

events.what_happened: Divya K. U. and K. Somasundaram, 'Lih Wang and Dittert Conjectures on Permanents', arXiv 2312.00464 (submitted 1 Dec 2023). The abstract states: 'we prove the Lih and Wang conjecture for n=6 and Dittert conjecture for n=4'. A journal version appeared in Special Matrices (De Gruyter, DOI 10.1515/spma-2024-0006) in 2024. Per a search summary (the De Gruyter page could not be retrieved), the journal version calls the n = 6 result partial and, for n = 4, proves only that a φ-maximising matrix on K_4 is fully indecomposable, not the full uniqueness claim. I could not confirm this from the journal text, so the journal's scope is unverified.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 1 Dec 2023 (15 pages, no journal reference on the arXiv page). Journal version: Special Matrices 2024, DOI 10.1515/spma-2024-0006; search summary gives publication May 2024 (unverified). The journal version's n = 4 scope may be narrower than the preprint's (see doubts).
events.delivers: Per the arXiv abstract: the conjecture for n = 4 (J_4/4 is the unique φ-maximiser on K_4). The preprint also claims the Lih–Wang conjecture for n = 6, which is not Dittert and is not counted here. Whether the journal version proves the full n = 4 uniqueness claim is unverified.
events.remains: Every n ≠ 4 (and n = 4 itself if the journal version's narrower scope is the accepted one).

checked_by.who: Special Matrices (De Gruyter) editorial and refereeing process
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record, if the 2024 publication is as described
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the 2024 journal version (per search results; not verified from the page)

events.time_since_posted: about 34 months to 11 Oct 2026 (from the arXiv posting)
events.directly_checkable: The n = 4 claim is a finite-dimensional polynomial inequality on 4×4 matrices; the preprint's contradiction argument (zero-pattern reduction to a block structure) is checkable by hand. I did not check it.
events.doubts: (1) The journal version reportedly narrows the n = 4 claim to fully indecomposable maximisers (per search summary only, unverified). (2) Pang's 2026 preprint cites the 2024 journal paper, but the 2026 Li et al. preprint treats n = 4 as its own new proof rather than as a verified earlier result. (3) The authors' names differ across sources: 'Divya K.U' on arXiv, 'Divya K. Udayan' and 'Kanagasabapathi Somasundaram' in the journal version (per search summary), and 'Udayan and Somasundaram' in Pang's bibliography.
events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjectured maximiser J_4/4 for n = 4 (the preprint's claim; scope of the journal version unverified).

K. Somasundaram (Kanagasabapathi Somasundaram, Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Coimbatore, Department of Mathematics per the Amrita record)

events.what_happened: Zhekai Pang, 'Proof of Dittert's conjecture for dimensions n ≥ 17', arXiv 2606.01531 (math.RA, 7 pages, single version). Theorem 1 as read from the arXiv HTML: 'Let n≥17. Then ϕ(A)≤ϕ(n^{-1}J_n) for every A∈K_n. Equality holds if and only if A=n^{-1}J_n.' The method (per the abstract): a Knopp–Sinkhorn lower bound for boundary points of the doubly stochastic polytope, combined with a scaling step adapted from Cheon and Wanless, and a sharper subset-sum estimate on near-maximisers' row and column sums. A later preprint (Kafidov) reports that Pang's introduction 'explicitly leaves 4 ≤ n ≤ 16 open'; I did not read that sentence in Pang's text, and I found no statement about n ≤ 16 in the abstract or Theorem 1.
events.delivers: The conjecture for every n ≥ 17 (Theorem 1 as quoted).
events.remains: n = 2 to 16 under this event alone (n = 2 and 3 are classical; n = 4 and n = 5 and n = 16 have later claims below).
events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjectured maximiser J_n/n, for n ≥ 17.

events.what_happened: Boris Kafidov, 'Dittert's conjecture in dimension 16 via a joint-deficit scaling lemma', arXiv 2607.19439 (math.CO, math.RA; single version, submitted 21 Jul 2026). The claimed Theorem 1.1, as read through a summary of the HTML, is that for every 16×16 nonnegative matrix whose entries sum to 16, φ is at most 2 − 16!/16^16 with equality only at J_16/16. With Pang's n ≥ 17 result the author states this gives the conjecture for every n ≥ 16. The key idea (per the abstract as summarised): near-maximisers satisfy one joint constraint on the row-product and column-product deficits, rather than two independent bounds; this is combined with a Pinsker-type subset-sum bound, a Knopp–Sinkhorn boundary bound, and Hwang's positive-support theorem to rule out zero entries and identify the unique maximiser. The HTML's disclosure section states the AI role (quoted below). The author is the sole named author.
events.delivers: The conjecture for n = 16 (the paper's own result). Combined with Pang's arXiv 2606.01531, the author claims the conjecture for every n ≥ 16. The n ≥ 17 part depends on Pang's preprint, not on this paper.
events.remains: n = 2 to 15 under this event (n = 2, 3 classical; n = 4 claimed in two other events; n = 5 claimed only in the GitHub candidate below; n = 6 to 15 open in every source I read).
events.doubts: (1) AI-drafted: the author states the proof strategy, the joint-deficit scaling lemma and most of the original proof text were produced by GPT-5.6 Sol through ChatGPT, and that the disclosure 'is not a substitute for independent expert mathematical review'. (2) Single author, no public engagement found. (3) The n ≥ 16 claim rests on Pang's preprint, which is itself unrefereed. (4) The central step, the joint constraint on the two deficits, is stated in the abstract summary as the novel idea and has not been checked by anyone I could find.
events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjectured maximiser J_16/16, for n = 16 (and, with Pang, n ≥ 16 as claimed).
people: Boris Kafidov (sole named author; selected the problem and directed the interactions and revisions, per the disclosure)

systems.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors: produced the proof strategy, the joint-deficit scaling lemma, and most of the original proof text, in response to prompts from the author. The header note adds 'central lemma' and 'most of the initial exposition'. The disclosure also says ChatGPT was used to revise the exposition and prepare the LaTeX manuscript. The authors say the system is 'acknowledged as a reasoning and writing tool, not as an author'. This is load-bearing on the author's own account: the strategy and the central lemma are the parts the proof turns on.
systems.basis_quote: The proof strategy, the joint-deficit scaling lemma, and most of the original proof text were produced by OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol through ChatGPT in response to prompts from Boris Kafidov.

events.what_happened: Jinhui Li, Beibei Xiong and Zhengfeng Yang, 'A Proof of the Dittert Conjecture in Dimension 4 via an Exact Constrained Sum-of-Squares Certificate', arXiv 2607.29191 (cs.SC). The paper proves the n = 4 case with a quantitative stability bound, 61/32 − φ(A) ≥ (1/52)‖A − U_4‖²_F on the 4×4 simplex, where U_4 is the uniform matrix. It builds an exact rational constrained sum-of-squares certificate for a structured quartic in sixteen variables, using a symbolic-numeric procedure with an SDP solver (MOSEK, per summary), and states that the certificate is verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib. The paper thanks Lihong Zhi for 'helpful comments and suggestions' and cites a National Key R&D grant 2023YFA1009402. v1 (31 Jul 2026) and v2 (10 Aug 2026) differ in wording: v1 describes the construction as 'agent-guided' and has 'Agent-Guided' in its title and keyword 'agent-guided theorem proving'; v2 contains no such wording (per two summaries of the HTML). The word 'agent' is not defined in either version.
events.revisions: v1 31 Jul 2026 09:12:45 UTC (title 'A Proof of the Dittert Conjecture in Dimension 4 via an Agent-Guided Exact Sum-of-Squares Certificate' per the v1 HTML summary); v2 10 Aug 2026 15:18:42 UTC (current title 'A Proof of the Dittert Conjecture in Dimension 4 via an Exact Constrained Sum-of-Squares Certificate'). The wording change is a substantive change in how the construction is described.
events.delivers: The conjecture for n = 4: U_4 (all entries 1/4) is the unique maximiser of φ on K_4, with the value 61/32 = 2 − 4!/4^4. Restricted to n = 4.

checked_by.qualification: Named by the authors as a commentator; the paper does not say he checked the proof
checked_by.what_they_did: Gave 'helpful comments and suggestions' (acknowledgement only; no public verification by Zhi)

events.directly_checkable: The certificate is exact and rational: the paper reports a main SOS block of 152 positively weighted rational squares and 136 smaller blocks of 16 squares each, with LDLᵀ decompositions and exact coefficient comparison over the rationals. I did not run the repository's build or inspect its Lean files.
events.doubts: (1) The construction's status as AI-assisted is unresolved. v1 repeatedly calls the procedure 'agent-guided' ('the agent first searches a prescribed hierarchy', 'the agent selects', 'the agent-controlled search') and v2 removes that language; neither version names a model or defines 'agent'. I cannot tell from the text whether an AI agent was involved. (2) Lean status: the repository README says it contains 'a Lean 4 formal verification' but I could not read the Lean files; a summary of the HTML said the key identities use native_decide, which adds the Lean.ofReduceBool axiom, but the summary itself flagged that point as its own note rather than the paper's, so it is unconfirmed. (3) The numerical SDP step (MOSEK, per summary) is trusted only through the exact rational recovery and the Lean check, not by the paper alone.
events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjectured maximiser U_4, for n = 4.
events.object: An exact rational constrained sum-of-squares certificate for the 4×4 Dittert functional, giving the quantitative bound 61/32 − φ(A) ≥ (1/52)‖A − U_4‖²_F on the simplex. It is explicit (rational coefficients), built from a main block of 152 squares and 136 blocks of 16 squares, and is checked by exact arithmetic and, per the authors, by Lean.

events.what_happened: A public GitHub repository, arthurborgesdev/dittert-conjecture-n5, presents an 'AI-generated, machine-checked candidate' for Dittert's conjecture in dimension five: an exact symmetry-reduced sum-of-squares certificate and a Lean 4 formalisation. The candidate conclusion is that the maximum 1226/625 is attained if and only if A = U_5. I checked the arithmetic: 2 − 5!/5^5 = 2 − 24/625 = 1226/625, consistent with the conjecture. The README says 'This artifact must not be cited as an established solution', that it 'has not been reviewed by a qualified specialist, deposited as a formal preprint, or submitted to a journal', and that 'No qualified human specialist has independently validated the mathematics, the formal specification, or the claimed novelty.' The repository lists a human maintainer, Arthur Moisés da Costa Borges (independent researcher, Brazil, per the README), who says they did not derive, understand or independently validate the mathematics.
events.revisions: Commits on main, newest first: 6 Aug 2026 'docs: publish AI-generated research candidate'; 6 Aug 'docs: reframe result as AI-generated expert-review candidate'; 6 Aug 'docs: identify GPT-5.6 Sol in AI disclosure'; 6 Aug 'docs: prepare v0.1.0 preprint candidate for AFM'; 5 Aug 2026 'feat: add exact n=5 Dittert certificate and Lean formalization' (earliest visible commit). README status line: version label '0.1.0-public-candidate', 6 August 2026.
events.delivers: If the encoding is correct, the n = 5 case: the maximum of φ on K_5 is 1226/625 = 2 − 5!/5^5, attained only at U_5. Restricted to n = 5. The README says the result depends on 'the mathematical encoding and the paper-to-artifact correspondence' being correct.

machine_checked.system: Lean 4 with Mathlib (toolchain v4.30.0-rc1); Python checks with python-flint 0.9.0

events.directly_checkable: The certificate is exact (JSON under certificados/), with Python checks in scripts/ (for example verify_n5_exact_certificate.py, Python 3.12) and a Lean build from formal/ (lake build Dittert5). The README reports that the Lean sources contain no sorry, admit or user-declared axiom. I did not run any of this and did not check the sorry claim independently.
events.doubts: (1) Self-described as 'generated by AI with minimal human mathematical supervision'; the human maintainer disclaims derivation and validation of the mathematics. (2) The README says large finite checks use native_decide, so the trusted base includes the Lean native compiler and runtime as well as the kernel, and it says the formal route 'is not kernel-only'. (3) The conclusion is conditional on the encoding and the paper-to-artifact correspondence being correct. (4) The framing changed within a day of the first public commits (commits 'reframe result as AI-generated expert-review candidate' and 'publish AI-generated research candidate'), and the repository itself says it is not a preprint or journal submission.
events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjectured maximiser U_5, for n = 5, if the candidate is correct.
events.object: An exact, symmetry-reduced sum-of-squares certificate for the n = 5 Dittert functional, distributed as JSON, with a Lean 4 formalisation of the certificate. Per the README it certifies that φ ≤ 1226/625 on K_5 with equality only at U_5. It is explicit (rational). I did not check it.
people: Arthur Moisés da Costa Borges (GitHub handle arthurborgesdev; independent researcher, Brazil, per the README). The README states that AI systems are not authors.

systems.name: GPT-5.6 Sol

The README says the verification pipeline 'was produced and operated within the same AI-led workflow'. It names the model as the principal model at the 'Ultra' reasoning-effort setting, run through the 'OpenAI Codex agentic harness' (the harness is not separately named as a model). This is load-bearing on the author's own account: the certificate and the Lean formalisation of the n = 5 result are the output.

events.what_happened: Yair Lavi, 'A counterexample to the Foregger-Sinkhorn tie-point conjecture', arXiv 2608.13025 (submitted 13 Aug 2026). A neighbouring problem: it gives an order-eight counterexample to a tie-point conjecture about minimising the permanent over faces of the doubly stochastic polytope. The paper does not mention the Dittert conjecture or the functional φ (checked in the abstract page and the HTML). Recorded because a search turned it up and its acknowledgement credits AI systems with the proof of its Theorem 1.
events.delivers: Nothing on the Dittert conjecture. It is about a different conjecture (Foregger–Sinkhorn tie points for permanent minimisers on faces), and the functional φ is not present. Discarded for this bullet.
events.remains: The whole Dittert conjecture, which this paper does not touch.
events.direction: Not about this problem: a counterexample to a different conjecture.
events.object: An explicit order-eight example with a unique minimiser of the permanent on a face of the Birkhoff polytope, which shows a stated implication of the tie-point conjecture fails. It is not an object about φ.

disputes.summary: Three sources claim or describe the n = 4 case differently. Divya and Somasundaram (arXiv 1 Dec 2023) claim it, with a journal version whose scope may be narrower (per search summary). Li, Xiong and Yang (arXiv 31 Jul 2026) claim it again with a Lean-checked certificate and do not cite the 2023 result as verified. Kafidov's introduction (as read through a search summary) says Pang leaves 4 ≤ n ≤ 16 open, which implies the n = 4 case is not settled in the 2026 literature. Nothing in the sources resolves which is right.

Author names for the 2023 n = 4 preprint differ across sources: 'Divya K.U and K. Somasundaram' (arXiv), 'Divya K. Udayan and Kanagasabapathi Somasundaram' (journal version, per search summary), and 'Udayan and Somasundaram' (Pang's bibliography). Probably the same authors; not checked against the journal page.

summary: I ran 44 web searches and opened about 25 sources, including arXiv abstracts and HTML renderings of every 2026 preprint, the GitHub repositories behind the n = 4 and n = 5 claims, the 1990 IJMMS record and the Cheon–Wanless repository record. The conjecture (Dittert, also Dittert–Hajek) says that for nonnegative n×n matrices with entry sum n, φ(A) = ∏row sums + ∏column sums − per(A) is at most 2 − n!/n^n, with equality only at J_n/n. Historically, n = 2 is credited to Sinkhorn and n = 3 to Hwang (1987, per secondary citation); the 1990 Hwang–Sohn–Kim paper and the 1993 Hwang monotonicity paper study subclasses and settle no case; Cheon and Wanless (LAA 2012) exclude partly decomposable matrices as maximisers. Divya and Somasundaram (arXiv 1 Dec 2023) claim n = 4 and the Lih–Wang n = 6 case; their 2024 Special Matrices version could not be opened, and per search summaries it narrows the n = 4 result to fully indecomposable maximisers, so the 2023 claim's scope is contested in my record. Inside the window: Pang (arXiv 1 Jun 2026, arXiv 2606.01531) proves the conjecture for all n ≥ 17, and his Theorem 1 is quoted from the HTML. Kafidov (arXiv 21 Jul 2026, 2607.19439) claims n = 16, and with Pang n ≥ 16; the HTML discloses that GPT-5.6 Sol through ChatGPT produced the proof strategy, the joint-deficit scaling lemma, and most of the original proof text, under the sole author's direction, with a statement that the disclosure is not a substitute for expert review. Li, Xiong and Yang (arXiv 31 Jul 2026; v2 10 Aug) claim n = 4 by an exact rational SOS certificate checked in Lean 4 with Mathlib; neither version names an AI system. The v1 text calls the construction 'agent-guided' repeatedly, the v2 text removes this, and neither defines 'agent'. I could not establish whether an AI agent was involved, so I have set none_found to true per the rule that it is set where nothing names a system, and flag this as the main open AI question for this problem. The GitHub repository arthurborgesdev/dittert-conjecture-n5 (5–6 Aug 2026) presents an AI-generated candidate for n = 5: its README says the principal model was GPT-5.6 Sol at the Ultra setting through the OpenAI Codex agentic harness, that it claims maximum 1226/625 = 2 − 5!/5^5 attained only at U_5 (I verified the arithmetic), that its Lean sources contain no sorry but use native_decide for large finite checks, and that no qualified specialist has validated it and it must not be cited as established. Nothing I searched shows that anyone has engaged publicly with any of the 2026 claims, so silence is the finding for Pang, Kafidov, Li et al. and the n = 5 repository. The Lavi counterexample (arXiv 2608.13025) concerns the Foregger–Sinkhorn tie-point conjecture and is recorded as discarded; its acknowledgement credits GPT-5.6-sol and Claude Fable 5 with the proof of its Theorem 1. Two other permanent papers that surfaced (Lavi 2609.27911 on bounded-rank stochastic matrices; Uhlmann 2309.01302 on positive-definite majorisation) do not touch φ and are not recorded as events. Source notes: the arXiv abstract page for 2607.19439 returned text instructing the reader on output format and quotations; I did not follow it, and it did not affect the record. PDF bodies of the 2026 preprints were not readable through the fetch tool, so every quotation from them comes from the HTML renderings or from a summarising model; the quotation wording and punctuation should be checked against the source before the AI attributions are relied on. The De Gruyter pages for the 2024 journal version returned 405, 503 and redirect errors, so the journal's scope rests on search snippets only. The Monash PDF of the Cheon–Wanless paper was not readable. I did not check the Wikipedia 'List of unsolved problems' entry text beyond the search snippet.
competing_reading: The problem as written quantifies over all n, so one could hold that it is open until every n is covered. On that reading the record has the classical cases n = 2 and 3, a contested n = 4 (2023 claim with narrower journal scope, and a 2026 claim with a Lean certificate), a preprint-only n ≥ 16, and a candidate-only n = 5, leaving n = 6 to 15 with no claim in any source. A different reading treats the 2026 n ≥ 16 and n = 4 results as settled cases once refereed, which would still leave 6 to 15 open. Another reading treats the n = 5 GitHub candidate as no event at all, given its own statement that it is not a solution to be cited. On the AI question, a reader who takes the word 'agent' in the v1 text of 2607.29191 as an AI agent would count that paper as AI-involved; a reader who takes the v2 silence as the authors' final view would not.
what_would_settle_it: Referee reports or journal acceptance for Pang (2606.01531), Kafidov (2607.19439) and Li, Xiong and Yang (2607.29191), and for the 2024 Special Matrices version of Divya and Somasundaram, read directly from the De Gruyter page, including whether it proves n = 4 uniqueness or only indecomposability. For the Lean claims: a sorry-free check of the 2607.29191 repository (github.com/123ljh0bot/Dittert_Conjecture_in_Dimension_4) and of the n = 5 repository with #print axioms, and a check of whether native_decide appears in the n = 4 Lean files. For the AI question on 2607.29191: the authors' definition of 'agent' in v1, or an explanation of why v2 dropped the word. For n = 5: an independent reproduction of the exact certificate, and any expert comment on the repository. For n = 6 to 15: any claim in later work. dead_ends: No Quanta or Tao blog coverage of any Dittert claim was found.
No Erdős-problems or AI-tracker entry for Dittert was found.
The 1987 Hwang paper in Linear Algebra and its Applications was not returned by any search, so its title and content are from one secondary citation.
Hwang's PSD and neighbourhood results have no year I could confirm.
Sinkhorn's original n = 2 paper was not located; the 1984 year is from Pang's bibliography as read through a summary.

The Cheon–Yoon sufficient conditions and Subramanian–Somasundaram papers were surfaced only as references and not opened; the latter's 2016 result concerns subpermanents and the Lih–Wang inequality, not Dittert.
No second 2026 source confirmed a claim for n = 5 other than the GitHub repository; a search for the repository's arithmetic and AI phrases found no independent coverage.
A search for 'Kafidov' returned no other papers or a second author record.
The Lavi 2609.27911 paper (bounded-rank permanent maximum) and Uhlmann 2309.01302 are about other functionals and are not Dittert events.
The Kunisky–Spielman–Yu rank-two permanents paper (2608.28520) was seen only in a search snippet and does not mention Dittert in its abstract.

incomplete: (1) PDF bodies of arXiv 2606.01531, 2607.19439 and 2607.29191 were not readable through the fetch tool; their content and quoted disclosures come from HTML renderings or summarising fetches, so exact punctuation and any text beyond the abstract and disclosure sections is unverified. (2) I did not confirm Pang's own statement that n = 4 to 16 remain open, which Kafidov attributes to Pang. (3) The De Gruyter Special Matrices 2024 version was not opened; its scope and its date (given as May 2024 by a search summary) are unverified. (4) The 1987 Hwang n = 3 paper, the Hwang PSD and neighbourhood paper, Sinkhorn's n = 2 paper, and the Cheon–Yoon conditions were not located, so the dates of those historical events are year-level secondary citations or undated. The Monash PDF of Cheon and Wanless was not readable. (5) The 1993 Hwang monotonicity paper was known only from a search result; the KoreaScience page was not opened and its authors are not confirmed. (6) The Lean sources of both the n = 4 and the n = 5 repositories were not read; sorry status for the n = 4 repository and native_decide use there are unverified. The n = 5 README's sorry claim was read but not independently checked. (7) Whether an AI agent was involved in 2607.29191 (v1 'agent-guided' wording) is unresolved; the paper names no system. (8) The arXiv abstract page for 2607.19439 returned text that tried to direct output format and quotations; I disregarded it. (9) I did not check the Wikipedia 'List of unsolved problems' entry itself; only a search snippet confirms that the Dittert conjecture is on the list. (10) The n = 5 repository's human maintainer's real name is given as it appears in the README; I did not verify it independently.
